## Purpose and interpretation

This draft evaluates the stored descriptive layer and builds a bounded all-talent
viewer co-participation network. The maintained relations provide:

1. **Viewer-video activity**: one row per talent, viewer, and video.
2. **Viewer profiles**: one row per talent and viewer.
3. **Global viewer profiles**: one row per stable viewer ID across all talents.

The report is read-only. Relation refreshes are owned by
`r_scripts/run/publish_viewer_activity.R`, not by the notebook.

The word *joined* needs qualification. The strongest date available for every
chatter is their **first observed chat** in the collected corpus. A public
YouTube subscription date is attached only when available. A
`membership_item` is an observed membership-related chat event, not an
authoritative paid-membership start date.

| Field | What it supports | What it does not prove |
|---|---|---|
| First observed chat | Earliest collected stream in which the viewer chatted | First watch, community membership, or historical first chat before collection |
| Public subscription date | Public subscription date visible in the latest subscriber snapshot | Paid membership or complete subscriber coverage |
| First membership event | Earliest collected `membership_item` for a viewer | Original paid-membership start or uninterrupted membership |
| Videos chatted in | Distinct collected videos containing at least one message | Videos watched without chatting |

## Parameters and setup

Use `talent_code` to inspect one exact talent code. A null value includes every
talent. Use `video_id` to display the chatter-level metrics for one video in
the selected scope. `profile_preview_limit` controls only displayed profile
tables; it does not change the calculations.

```{r}
#| label: setup

required_packages <- c(
  "DBI", "duckdb", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "here", "knitr", "scales", "tidyr"
)
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Install the required R packages before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))

source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "repo_env.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "datalake_root.r"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "db_connect.R"))

load_repo_env(repo_root = here::here())
db_path <- talent_lakehouse_db_path()
if (!file.exists(db_path)) {
  stop("Unified talent lakehouse not found: ", db_path, call. = FALSE)
}

con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)

normalize_parameter <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L || is.na(value[[1]])) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  value <- trimws(as.character(value[[1]]))
  if (nzchar(value)) value else NULL
}

talent_code <- normalize_parameter(params$talent_code)
video_id <- normalize_parameter(params$video_id)
profile_preview_limit <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$profile_preview_limit))
if (is.na(profile_preview_limit) || profile_preview_limit < 1L) {
  profile_preview_limit <- 50L
}
network_max_nodes <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$network_max_nodes))
network_min_videos <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$network_min_videos))
network_min_shared_videos <- suppressWarnings(
  as.integer(params$network_min_shared_videos)
)
network_label_count <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(params$network_label_count))
if (is.na(network_max_nodes) || network_max_nodes < 2L) network_max_nodes <- 75L
if (is.na(network_min_videos) || network_min_videos < 1L) network_min_videos <- 3L
if (is.na(network_min_shared_videos) || network_min_shared_videos < 1L) {
  network_min_shared_videos <- 2L
}
if (is.na(network_label_count) || network_label_count < 0L) {
  network_label_count <- 15L
}

talent_filter_sql <- if (is.null(talent_code)) {
  ""
} else {
  "AND activity.talent_code = ?"
}
talent_query_params <- if (is.null(talent_code)) list() else list(talent_code)

display_table <- function(rows, digits = 1L) {
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) {
    return(knitr::kable(data.frame(message = "No rows matched.")))
  }
  knitr::kable(rows, digits = digits)
}

ggplot2::theme_set(
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom"
    )
)

scope_label <- if (is.null(talent_code)) "All talents" else talent_code
display_table(data.frame(
  item = c("Database", "Talent scope", "Network scope", "Rendered at"),
  value = c(
    db_path,
    scope_label,
    "All talents",
    format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", tz = "UTC")
  )
))
```

## Data preflight

The prototype depends only on canonical chat, video, talent, and public
subscriber relations. It deliberately does not use generated analysis files.

```{r}
#| label: data-preflight

required_relations <- data.frame(
  schema_name = c(
    "text", "catalog", "catalog", "clean", "analysis", "analysis", "analysis"
  ),
  relation_name = c(
    "chat_messages", "videos", "talents", "public_subscriber_snapshots",
    "viewer_video_activity", "viewer_profiles", "global_viewer_profiles"
  )
)

relation_status <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT table_schema AS schema_name, table_name AS relation_name",
    "FROM information_schema.tables",
    "WHERE (table_schema, table_name) IN (",
    "  ('text', 'chat_messages'),",
    "  ('catalog', 'videos'),",
    "  ('catalog', 'talents'),",
    "  ('clean', 'public_subscriber_snapshots'),",
    "  ('analysis', 'viewer_video_activity'),",
    "  ('analysis', 'viewer_profiles'),",
    "  ('analysis', 'global_viewer_profiles')",
    ")"
  )
)

required_relations <- required_relations %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    relation_status %>% dplyr::mutate(available = TRUE),
    by = c("schema_name", "relation_name")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    available = dplyr::coalesce(.data$available, FALSE),
    status = dplyr::if_else(.data$available, "PASS", "FAIL")
  )

display_table(required_relations[, c("status", "schema_name", "relation_name")])
if (!all(required_relations$available)) {
  stop(
    "Required lakehouse relations are missing. Run the viewer activity ",
    "publisher before rendering this report.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```

## Load viewer-video activity

`message_timestamp` is intentionally excluded from date calculations because
replay chat sources can encode it as an epoch-relative clock. The stream date
comes from `actual_start_at`, falling back to `published_at`; the first and last
message offsets remain available in seconds.

```{r}
#| label: load-viewer-video-activity

viewer_video_sql <- paste(
  "SELECT",
  "  activity.talent_code,",
  "  talent.talent_name,",
  "  activity.channel_id,",
  "  activity.video_id,",
  "  video.title AS video_title,",
  "  activity.user_id,",
  "  activity.latest_username_in_video,",
  "  activity.stream_at,",
  "  activity.message_count,",
  "  activity.text_message_count,",
  "  activity.paid_message_count,",
  "  activity.membership_event_count,",
  "  activity.first_message_second,",
  "  activity.last_message_second,",
  "  activity.active_span_seconds,",
  "  activity.pipeline_run_id,",
  "  activity.calculated_at",
  "FROM analysis.viewer_video_activity AS activity",
  "JOIN catalog.videos AS video",
  "  USING (talent_code, channel_id, video_id)",
  "JOIN catalog.talents AS talent",
  "  USING (talent_code)",
  "WHERE 1 = 1",
  talent_filter_sql,
  "ORDER BY activity.talent_code, activity.stream_at,",
  "  activity.video_id, activity.user_id"
)

viewer_video_activity <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  viewer_video_sql,
  params = talent_query_params
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    stream_at = as.POSIXct(.data$stream_at, tz = "UTC"),
    active_minutes = .data$active_span_seconds / 60,
    messages_per_active_minute = dplyr::if_else(
      .data$active_minutes > 0,
      .data$message_count / .data$active_minutes,
      as.numeric(.data$message_count)
    )
  )

if (nrow(viewer_video_activity) == 0L) {
  stop("No valid chat activity matched the selected scope.", call. = FALSE)
}

display_table(
  viewer_video_activity %>%
    dplyr::select(
      .data$talent_code,
      .data$video_id,
      .data$stream_at,
      .data$user_id,
      .data$latest_username_in_video,
      .data$message_count,
      .data$first_message_second,
      .data$last_message_second
    ) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 10L)
)
```

## Load overall viewer profiles

The latest observed username is a label; the stable profile key is
`(talent_code, user_id)`. Public subscription records use the value in the
latest snapshot. `subscription_date_versions` exposes cases where the reported
date changed across snapshots rather than silently treating the history as
stable.

```{r}
#| label: load-viewer-profiles

viewer_profile_sql <- paste(
  "SELECT",
  "  profile.*,",
  "  talent.talent_name,",
  "  profile.public_subscribed_at AS subscribed_at,",
  "  profile.public_subscriber_snapshot_date AS snapshot_date",
  "FROM analysis.viewer_profiles AS profile",
  "JOIN catalog.talents AS talent USING (talent_code)",
  "WHERE 1 = 1",
  if (is.null(talent_code)) "" else "AND profile.talent_code = ?",
  "ORDER BY profile.talent_code, profile.user_id"
)

viewer_profiles <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  viewer_profile_sql,
  params = talent_query_params
) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    observed_span_days = as.numeric(
      difftime(
        .data$last_observed_stream_at,
        .data$first_observed_stream_at,
        units = "days"
      )
    )
  )
```

## Overall corpus coverage

These figures describe only chats that were collected and successfully joined
to cataloged videos.

```{r}
#| label: corpus-coverage

talent_summary <- viewer_profiles %>%
  dplyr::group_by(.data$talent_code, .data$talent_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    chatters = dplyr::n(),
    videos_with_chat = dplyr::n_distinct(
      viewer_video_activity$video_id[
        viewer_video_activity$talent_code == dplyr::first(.data$talent_code)
      ]
    ),
    messages = sum(.data$total_messages),
    median_videos_per_chatter = stats::median(.data$videos_chatted_in),
    median_messages_per_chatter = stats::median(.data$total_messages),
    public_subscription_matches = sum(.data$public_subscription_matched),
    public_subscription_coverage = mean(.data$public_subscription_matched),
    chatters_with_membership_events = sum(.data$membership_events > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

display_table(
  talent_summary %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      messages = scales::comma(.data$messages),
      public_subscription_coverage = scales::percent(
        .data$public_subscription_coverage,
        accuracy = 0.1
      )
    )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: subscription-coverage-plot
#| fig-height: 4.5

ggplot2::ggplot(
  talent_summary,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = stats::reorder(.data$talent_code, .data$public_subscription_coverage),
    y = .data$public_subscription_coverage
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#3B82F6", width = 0.7) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    ggplot2::aes(
      label = scales::percent(.data$public_subscription_coverage, accuracy = 0.1)
    ),
    hjust = -0.1,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, max(talent_summary$public_subscription_coverage) * 1.2)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Public subscription dates cover a minority of observed chatters",
    subtitle = "Coverage uses each subscriber's latest available snapshot record",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of observed chatters with a public subscription match"
  )
```

## When chatters first appeared

This is the recommended first view of community entry. Each viewer is counted
once, in the month of their earliest collected chat stream.

```{r}
#| label: first-observed-cohorts

first_observed_cohorts <- viewer_profiles %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    first_observed_month = as.Date(
      format(.data$first_observed_stream_at, "%Y-%m-01")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::count(
    .data$talent_code,
    .data$talent_name,
    .data$first_observed_month,
    name = "newly_observed_chatters"
  )

ggplot2::ggplot(
  first_observed_cohorts,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = .data$first_observed_month,
    y = .data$newly_observed_chatters
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#7C3AED", width = 25) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ggplot2::vars(.data$talent_code),
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "First observed chatters by month",
    subtitle = "A collection-bounded entry cohort, not a complete community join date",
    x = "First observed chat month",
    y = "Newly observed chatters"
  )
```

## Breadth and intensity of participation

The log scales keep occasional and highly active chatters visible in the same
view. Color marks whether a public subscription date is available; it should
not be interpreted as subscriber versus non-subscriber status.

```{r}
#| label: participation-scatter
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot2::ggplot(
  viewer_profiles,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = .data$videos_chatted_in,
    y = .data$total_messages,
    color = .data$public_subscription_matched
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 1.4) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ggplot2::vars(.data$talent_code),
    scales = "free",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = "#9CA3AF", `TRUE` = "#F59E0B"),
    labels = c(`FALSE` = "No public match", `TRUE` = "Public match")
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Participation breadth and message intensity",
    x = "Distinct videos chatted in (log scale)",
    y = "Total messages (log scale)",
    color = "Public subscription record"
  )
```

## Video-level activity

The first table identifies the videos with the most observed chat activity.
When `video_id` is supplied, the second table answers how many messages each
viewer sent in that video, along with their first and last offsets.

```{r}
#| label: video-activity

video_summary <- viewer_video_activity %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    .data$talent_code,
    .data$video_id,
    .data$video_title,
    .data$stream_at
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    chatters = dplyr::n_distinct(.data$user_id),
    messages = sum(.data$message_count),
    paid_messages = sum(.data$paid_message_count),
    membership_events = sum(.data$membership_event_count),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$messages))

display_table(video_summary %>% dplyr::slice_head(n = 20L))

if (!is.null(video_id)) {
  selected_video_activity <- viewer_video_activity %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$video_id == video_id) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(.data$message_count),
      .data$user_id
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      .data$talent_code,
      .data$video_id,
      .data$user_id,
      .data$latest_username_in_video,
      .data$message_count,
      .data$text_message_count,
      .data$paid_message_count,
      .data$membership_event_count,
      .data$first_message_second,
      .data$last_message_second,
      .data$active_minutes
    ) %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = profile_preview_limit)

  if (nrow(selected_video_activity) == 0L) {
    warning("The requested video_id did not match the selected scope: ", video_id)
  }
  print(display_table(selected_video_activity))
}
```

## All-talent core chatter network

The global network treats two viewers as connected when they chatted in the
same video for any talent. Edge weight is the number of distinct videos they
shared across the full lakehouse. This is a co-participation network: it does not show
direct replies, friendship, or proof that the viewers know one another.

The stored global profile supplies reusable node metadata. Network thresholds
and centrality are calculated at render time because they belong to this
specific network definition.

```{r}
#| label: global-profile-summary

global_profiles <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
  con,
  paste(
    "SELECT *",
    "FROM analysis.global_viewer_profiles",
    "ORDER BY talents_chatted_with DESC, videos_chatted_in DESC,",
    "  total_messages DESC, user_id"
  )
)

if (nrow(global_profiles) == 0L) {
  stop("No stored global viewer profiles are available.", call. = FALSE)
}

global_summary <- global_profiles %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    observed_chatters = dplyr::n(),
    cross_talent_chatters = sum(.data$cross_talent_chatter),
    maximum_talent_reach = max(.data$talents_chatted_with),
    cross_talent_share = mean(.data$cross_talent_chatter),
    median_active_videos = stats::median(.data$videos_chatted_in),
    median_messages = stats::median(.data$total_messages)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    cross_talent_share = scales::percent(.data$cross_talent_share, accuracy = 0.1)
  )

display_table(global_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: global-network-build

network_candidates <- global_profiles %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$videos_chatted_in >= network_min_videos) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(
    dplyr::desc(.data$talents_chatted_with),
    dplyr::desc(.data$videos_chatted_in),
    dplyr::desc(.data$total_messages),
    .data$user_id
  ) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = network_max_nodes)

candidate_placeholders <- paste(rep("?", nrow(network_candidates)), collapse = ", ")

if (nrow(network_candidates) >= 2L) {
  global_presence <- DBI::dbGetQuery(
    con,
    paste0(
      "SELECT DISTINCT talent_code, video_id, user_id ",
      "FROM analysis.viewer_video_activity ",
      "WHERE user_id IN (", candidate_placeholders, ")"
    ),
    params = as.list(network_candidates$user_id)
  )

  global_edges <- global_presence %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      global_presence,
      by = c("talent_code", "video_id"),
      suffix = c("_from", "_to"),
      relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$user_id_from < .data$user_id_to) %>%
    dplyr::count(
      from = .data$user_id_from,
      to = .data$user_id_to,
      name = "shared_videos"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data$shared_videos >= network_min_shared_videos)
} else {
  global_edges <- data.frame(
    from = character(),
    to = character(),
    shared_videos = integer()
  )
}

network_user_ids <- sort(unique(c(global_edges$from, global_edges$to)))
network_nodes <- network_candidates %>%
  dplyr::filter(.data$user_id %in% network_user_ids) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(.data$user_id)

if (nrow(network_nodes) >= 2L && nrow(global_edges) > 0L) {
  node_index <- stats::setNames(seq_len(nrow(network_nodes)), network_nodes$user_id)
  adjacency <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = nrow(network_nodes),
    ncol = nrow(network_nodes),
    dimnames = list(network_nodes$user_id, network_nodes$user_id)
  )
  from_index <- unname(node_index[global_edges$from])
  to_index <- unname(node_index[global_edges$to])
  adjacency[cbind(from_index, to_index)] <- global_edges$shared_videos
  adjacency[cbind(to_index, from_index)] <- global_edges$shared_videos

  eigen_result <- eigen(adjacency, symmetric = TRUE)
  eigenvector_centrality <- abs(eigen_result$vectors[, 1])
  if (max(eigenvector_centrality) > 0) {
    eigenvector_centrality <- eigenvector_centrality / max(eigenvector_centrality)
  }

  graph_distance <- matrix(Inf, nrow(adjacency), ncol(adjacency))
  diag(graph_distance) <- 0
  connected <- adjacency > 0
  graph_distance[connected] <- 1 / sqrt(adjacency[connected])
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(graph_distance))) {
    graph_distance <- pmin(
      graph_distance,
      outer(graph_distance[, k], graph_distance[k, ], "+")
    )
  }
  finite_max <- max(graph_distance[is.finite(graph_distance)])
  graph_distance[!is.finite(graph_distance)] <- finite_max * 2

  if (nrow(network_nodes) == 2L) {
    coordinates <- matrix(c(-1, 0, 1, 0), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  } else {
    coordinates <- stats::cmdscale(
      stats::as.dist(graph_distance),
      k = 2,
      eig = FALSE
    )
  }

  network_nodes <- network_nodes %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      x = coordinates[, 1],
      y = coordinates[, 2],
      degree = rowSums(adjacency > 0),
      weighted_degree = rowSums(adjacency),
      eigenvector_centrality = eigenvector_centrality
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(
      dplyr::desc(.data$eigenvector_centrality),
      dplyr::desc(.data$weighted_degree),
      dplyr::desc(.data$talents_chatted_with),
      dplyr::desc(.data$total_messages)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(core_rank = dplyr::row_number())

  coordinate_lookup <- network_nodes %>%
    dplyr::select(.data$user_id, .data$x, .data$y)
  network_edges_plot <- global_edges %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      coordinate_lookup,
      by = c("from" = "user_id")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x_from = .data$x, y_from = .data$y) %>%
    dplyr::inner_join(
      coordinate_lookup,
      by = c("to" = "user_id")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(x_to = .data$x, y_to = .data$y)
} else {
  network_edges_plot <- data.frame()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: global-network-plot
#| fig-height: 8

if (nrow(network_edges_plot) == 0L) {
  plot.new()
  graphics::text(
    0.5,
    0.5,
    paste(
      "No all-talent network survived the current thresholds.",
      "Reduce network_min_videos or network_min_shared_videos."
    )
  )
} else {
  label_nodes <- network_nodes %>%
    dplyr::slice_head(n = min(network_label_count, nrow(network_nodes)))

  global_network_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      data = network_edges_plot,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$x_from,
        y = .data$y_from,
        xend = .data$x_to,
        yend = .data$y_to,
        linewidth = .data$shared_videos
      ),
      color = "#94A3B8",
      alpha = 0.25
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      data = network_nodes,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$x,
        y = .data$y,
        size = .data$eigenvector_centrality,
        color = .data$talents_chatted_with
      ),
      alpha = 0.9
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
      data = label_nodes,
      ggplot2::aes(
        x = .data$x,
        y = .data$y,
        label = dplyr::coalesce(.data$current_username, .data$user_id)
      ),
      nudge_y = 0.04,
      check_overlap = TRUE,
      size = 3
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_linewidth_continuous(
      trans = "sqrt",
      range = c(0.2, 2.2),
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(2.5, 11)) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1) +
    ggplot2::coord_equal() +
    ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Core chatter co-participation network across all talents",
      subtitle = paste(
        "Candidates:", network_max_nodes,
        "| Minimum active videos:", network_min_videos,
        "| Minimum shared videos per edge:", network_min_shared_videos
      ),
      size = "Eigenvector centrality",
      color = "Talents chatted with"
    )

  print(global_network_plot)
}
```

## Candidate persistent design

The maintained grains are:

| Candidate relation | Key | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `viewer_video_activity` | `(talent_code, video_id, user_id)` | Message counts, event counts, first/last offsets, and active span within a video |
| `viewer_profiles` | `(talent_code, user_id)` | First/latest observed activity, distinct active videos, lifetime observed counts, and latest display label |
| `global_viewer_profiles` | `user_id` | Cross-talent reach, all-talent activity totals, primary talent, subscription coverage, and reusable node attributes |

Public subscription evidence should remain joined from
`clean.public_subscriber_snapshots` or be represented with explicit snapshot
lineage. It should not silently become a universal viewer join date.

Viewer edges remain ephemeral and definition-specific. Remaining decisions are:

- whether bot/moderator/owner accounts need exclusion flags;
- whether deleted or unavailable videos remain in lifetime counts;
- whether membership events require a separate event-level analytical view;
- whether the current full refresh should later become incremental;
- which collection-coverage fields must accompany first-observed dates.
